method: Every finding was produced by a command run against the checked-out repository or the GitHub API on 2026-11-27, after rebasing onto main at 76b22b8. Line numbers refer to that commit. Findings that could no longer be reproduced were removed rather than carried forward.
headline: Re-audited after the root dashboard was replaced by the integration session (PR #22). The four line-level defects this reviewer originally logged against the old root index.html — conflicting hotel prices, an unsourced '~15–20 minute' travel claim, a wrong MICHELIN reveal date and a '3–4 nights' span for a 3-night window — no longer exist in the tree, so they have been retired rather than repeated. What remains are structural issues that still hold today.

findings.title: Two independent build systems publish to the same Pages URL
findings.evidence: The GitHub Pages API reports build_type 'legacy' with source branch 'main' and path '/', while .github/workflows/pages.yml line 27 uploads 'path: docs' as an artifact deployment. Both mechanisms target the same site, so which content a visitor receives depends on deployment ordering rather than on a single source of truth.
findings.impact: A stale legacy build can silently override a newer artifact deploy (or the reverse), and neither pipeline guards the other. Any future move to a custom domain or branch change has two places to update.
findings.how_to_fix: Disable the legacy branch source in repository settings and keep only the Actions deployment in pages.yml.

findings.title: CI does not validate the pages it deploys
findings.evidence: The three validators in .github/workflows (pages-check.yml:23, validate.yml:29, validate-field-notes.yml:27) assert only against docs/session-059c3126, docs/session-b29fc34e and docs/session-2e5e3452. Root *.html and docs/*.html — the pages a visitor actually lands on — are rebuilt and compared by nothing.
findings.impact: A regression on the landing page or any category page can merge with every check green. The session pages are the best-tested artifacts in the repository; the front door is the least-tested.
findings.how_to_fix: Add one job that rebuilds the root site from its generator and fails on `git diff --exit-code`, the same pattern already used for the three session directories.

findings.title: Published session archive still asserts a superseded star count
findings.evidence: docs/session-36cc5108/flagged.html contains the phrase 'three starred'. The current 2026 MICHELIN Guide Southwest selection has four starred Las Vegas restaurants (two-star Joël Robuchon plus one-star é, Guy Savoy and L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon).
findings.impact: An archived page contradicts the live selection on a fact a traveller is likely to plan around. Because the archive is published and indexable, the error is reachable without any warning that it is historical.
findings.how_to_fix: Either correct the archived page or add a dated banner marking it superseded, and point readers to the current MICHELIN page.

findings.title: No LICENSE file
findings.evidence: `ls LICENSE*` returns nothing at the repository root. No licence text appears in README.md either.
findings.impact: Without an explicit grant, default copyright applies: the content is technically all-rights-reserved and third parties cannot safely reuse it. It also leaves the provenance of the aggregated research ambiguous.
findings.how_to_fix: Add a LICENSE file (or a short 'all rights reserved' statement) so the terms are explicit.

findings.title: Root site and docs/ subsites do not link to each other
findings.evidence: A crawl of the 7 root *.html pages finds 0 hrefs into docs/, and a crawl of docs/*.html finds 0 hrefs back up to the root. The two halves of the published site are reachable only by typing a URL.
findings.impact: Five session subsites and the canonical dashboard form two disconnected islands. A visitor who lands deep in docs/ has no route back to the main planner.
findings.how_to_fix: Add a single persistent 'back to planner' link in each subsite header, and a 'research archive' link on the root.

findings.title: Historical snapshots live inside the deployed tree
findings.evidence: docs/session-legacy-root/ holds a full copy of a previous root dashboard (activities, flagged-for-review, hotels, index, questions, restaurants, suggestions) plus a main-0d3e73e snapshot. Because pages.yml uploads all of docs/, these archives are published and indexable.
findings.impact: Superseded pages stay publicly reachable and compete with current content in search results, while also inflating every deployment artifact.
findings.how_to_fix: Move archives outside docs/ (or exclude them in the workflow) and keep one clearly-labelled snapshot per merge.

findings.title: Root pages are very long single-line HTML
findings.evidence: index.html lines 41–46 each contain an entire table section on one physical line (the hotel and restaurant blocks are single lines several thousand characters long).
findings.impact: Line-anchored code review and git blame are effectively impossible for those regions; any edit rewrites a whole line. It also makes the file hostile to line-based diff review.
findings.how_to_fix: Emit one element per line from the generator so diffs and blame stay readable.

clean_checks: 0 broken local references across every HTML file in docs/** (40 pages checked by regex crawl).
0 broken local references across the 7 root HTML pages.
No loopback-host strings, placeholder lorem text, or developer code markers in any published HTML, JS or CSS under docs/, assets/ or field-notes/.
python3 scripts/check_site.py, validate_field_notes.py and check_session_b29fc34e.py all exit 0.
GitHub Pages is enabled, public, HTTPS-enforced, and the latest build status is 'built'.

The four line-level defects previously logged against the old root index.html (conflicting prices, unsourced travel time, wrong reveal date, wrong night span) are no longer present and have been retired from this list.
